o.text: From Old Anatolian Turkish بَبَا, ultimately an onomatopoeic reduplication.
Ultimately from Proto-Turkic *yaman (“bad, wicked; sickness, inflammation”).
From Arabic قُوَّة (quwwa). Doublet of qüvvə.

From Proto-Turkic *tï̄n, whence also Azerbaijani dincəlmək (“to rest”) and dinc (“quite, peaceful”). Cognate with Bashkir тынсыу (tınsıw), Tatar тынчу (tınçu), Kazakh тыншу (tınšuw, “stuffy, poorly ventilated”), Kumyk тунчукъ (tunçuq, “stuffy, poorly ventilated”).
